policy: Disagreements are listed with a resolution. Nothing taught was chosen silently.

items.freeDictionary: phonetics empty in the 2026-10-29 API payload; not used
items.disagreement: Sources agree both exist, but they rank the primary differently in casual teaching materials. CMU's first entry and Wiktionary's main GA form are voiced /wɪð/.
items.resolution: The word card teaches /wɪð/. A separate drill card with-prep-voiceless teaches /wɪθ/ and is labelled as the less common final variant, because J1's sound focus is /θ/. This is not a silent pick.

items.disagreement: CMU has only /ʃʊr/. Free Dictionary's US audio line is /ʃɔɹ/, the pour-poor merger.
items.resolution: Teach /ʃʊr/ to match CMUdict and Piper en-us. The card notes /ʃɔr/ as an accepted US merger variant. Audio is the /ʃʊr/ form.

items.disagreement: Primary vowel is not unique across US sources.
items.resolution: Teach CMU's first entry /wɑnt/, which Wiktionary and Free Dictionary also list. Audio is phoneme-forced to /wɑnt/ so it matches the card. /wɔnt/ stays as a labelled variant.

items.disagreement: Both /hə/ and /hɛ/ onsets are standard. Rank differs.
items.resolution: Teach CMU's first entry /həˈloʊ/. Card lists /hɛˈloʊ/ as a variant.

items.disagreement: CMU writes the NEAR vowel as IY, so a naive map is /hir/. Learner dictionaries usually write /hɪr/.
items.resolution: Display /hɪr/. The converter treats IY immediately before R as the NEAR vowel. This matches Free Dictionary's /hɪɹ/ and does not invent a second sense.
Teach CMU's first entry /sɑft/. Audio forced to /sɑft/. /sɔft/ noted as a variant. British /sɒft/ is not taught.

items.disagreement: Free Dictionary returned only the two-syllable variant. CMU and Wiktionary's first form are one syllable.
items.resolution: Teach one-syllable /smaɪl/. The two-syllable form is noted, not used for audio.

items.freeDictionary: API payload missed the article and showed only /ði/
items.disagreement: Not a real US disagreement. The API record was incomplete.
items.resolution: Two cards: the-art /ðə/ before consonants, the-art-vowel /ði/ before vowels. Strong /ðiː/ noted. The before-vowel clip is [[ðˈi]] aisle seat is free. A leading orthographic The made Piper say /ðə/ and then /ði/.

items.disagreement: Free Dictionary returned the NZ vowel. US sources agree on /ðɪs/.
API missed the noun. CMUdict and Wiktionary agree on the split.
items.resolution: wind-noun /wɪnd/ with carrier 'The wind is strong tonight.' wind-verb /waɪnd/ with carrier 'Wind the clock tonight.' Audio is phoneme-forced so the sense cannot flip.

cmudict: jewelry JH UW1 L R IY0 and JH UW1 AH0 L R IY0
items.disagreement: Spelling gap in CMUdict, not a sound conflict.
items.resolution: Map jewellery to CMU jewelry's two-syllable entry JH UW1 L R IY0. The card teaches /ˈdʒul.ɹi/. Piper's default reading of the spelling is the three-syllable variant, so every teaching clip is phoneme-forced to [[dʒˈulɹi]]. The three-syllable /ˈdʒu.əl.ɹi/ stays a noted variant and is not what the mp3 says.

items.freeDictionary: CMUdict is the US source for this pair
items.disagreement: CMU's first entry is /jɔɹ/. The shipped clip says /jʊɹ/.
items.resolution: Keep the headword at Y UH1 R /ˈjʊɹ/ so the card matches the existing mp3. List CMU's first entry /jɔɹ/ as a variant. Not a silent drop.

items.disagreement: The citation form is /tu/. The only shipped clip, 'I am flying to Hong Kong,' is the weak /tə/.
items.resolution: The headword is weak /tə/ (CMU T AH0, stress 0) so the example button matches the mp3. Strong /tu/ and weak /tɪ/ are variants. The sentence was not re-forced to a stressed [[tˈu]].

items.disagreement: None. Recorded because the lesson brief names /ʃ/ next to check-in, and that would be the wrong phoneme.
items.resolution: check-in is taught as /ˈtʃɛk ɪn/. The /ʃ/ drill uses sure, show, information, sheet. Learners are told check is /tʃ/, not /ʃ/.
